content:
Sean Gallagher: PIR / post-incident review for yesterday’s demo outage (429s). Threading here so we can keep updates + action items in one place.

Sean Gallagher: Incident summary
- What happened: Demo tenant started returning HTTP 429s during a live customer call. Impacted chat completions + streaming (requests rejected before stream started).
- Who/where: Sales demo tenant (NA region). Reported by SEs in real time.
- Duration (customer-visible): ~8–10 min of “hard fail” until we lowered request rate + bumped quota. Residual ~15 min of “we’re watching it” while dashboards caught up.
- Severity: Demo Sev2 (per our demo SLO policy).
- Tracking: SUP-4127 (customer-support style ticket), plus follow-ups in ENG-4862 / ENG-4879.

Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Demo Sev2 created by @sean_gallagher. Channel: #eng-sre. Impact: demo tenant 429 throttling during live call. Commander: @sean_gallagher.

Sean Gallagher: Timeline (approx)
- T0: SE starts scripted workload + a couple of parallel “live” pokes from AE. 429s begin.
- T+2m: #sales flags “getting throttled” + screenshots of 429 responses.
- T+5m: We confirm quota/rate-limit config wasn’t aligned w/ the new synthetic traffic generator baseline.
- T+8m: Temporary mitigation: throttle demo runner, request quota bump, retry.
- T+10m: Demo resumes w/ reduced concurrency.

Sean Gallagher: Root cause (current best understanding)
- Demo tenant default quotas (RPS + tokens/min) were set assuming single-session usage.
- In practice, the demo environment now has:
  1) synthetic traffic generator (to keep Console populated),
  2) SE demo runner (scripted scenario),
  3) occasional parallel demos / “someone else testing”.
- Those stacked loads pushed us over the per-project rate limit, triggering 429s.
- Healthcheck endpoint reported “OK” because it only checked model availability + dashboard ingestion, not quota headroom / current throttling.

Sean Gallagher: Contributing factors
- The new traffic generator preset is “realistic” but we didn’t re-validate quotas after enabling it by default.
- Lack of a clear “parallel demo” guardrail (separate projects/keys or enforced namespaces) meant cross-demo noise.
- Console dashboards lagged; SEs couldn’t quickly tell if 429s were from their workload vs background traffic.

Sean Gallagher: What went well
- Field team escalated quickly with concrete error output.
- Mitigation was straightforward once we found the limiter.
- We already have a demo-only healthcheck endpoint in-flight; we can extend it rather than inventing net-new.

Sean Gallagher: What went poorly
- Healthcheck gave a false sense of safety (green but no quota signal).
- Quota defaults weren’t aligned to demo reality.
- We didn’t have a single “stop synthetic traffic now” button documented for SEs.

Sean Gallagher: Action items (proposal)
1) Quota defaults
  - Increase demo tenant project quotas to support: 1 SE demo + synthetic traffic + 1 “accidental” parallel load.
  - Add explicit caps so we don’t melt shared infra; tune to SLO targets.
  - Owner: Ethan (control plane) + Devon (automation) + Sean (SRE review)
  - Due: end of week

2) Healthcheck: include quota headroom + recent 429s
  - Add checks:
    - current effective rate-limit config (RPS + tokens/min)
    - last 5 min 429 count > threshold => FAIL
    - estimated headroom given current background traffic
  - Output should be SE-readable (PASS/FAIL + “why”).
  - Owner: Allison + Logan
  - Due: next week

3) Synthetic traffic generator: “demo mode” preset + pause/runbook
  - Reduce baseline concurrency during business hours.
  - Document kill switch + expected recovery time for dashboards.
  - Owner: Mei
  - Due: next week

4) Operational guardrails: prevent cross-demo contamination
  - Push on ENG-4894 path: per-demo project namespaces + scoped keys.
  - In the interim: a documented convention for booking “demo slots” + which project to use.
  - Owner: Markus + Talia

5) Sales-facing runbook updates
  - Update reset + preflight checklist: run healthcheck, verify headroom, verify synthetic traffic state.
  - Add “if you see 429” immediate steps.
  - Owner: Markus (with Sean review)

Sean Gallagher: Please reply with (a) corrections to RC/timeline, (b) anything we missed, (c) confirm owners/dates. :eyes:

Allison Grant: +1 to adding “recent 429s” to healthcheck. We can also wire an alert on demo project 429 rate to the demo on-call alias (not #sales). The false-green check is the big pain.

Ethan Park: Agree RC. The quota config was still the old baseline. I can bump demo org/project quotas + ensure bootstrap applies it idempotently. I’d like to keep a hard ceiling to avoid “demo tenant becomes a load test”.

Markus Klein: From the SE side: we had 2 people poking the demo tenant while I was running the scripted scenario (not intentional, just someone testing the deck). So yeah, we need better isolation or at least a “please don’t use project X” norm.

Devon Price: I can add quota config to the bootstrap CLI so it’s always set on reset (and printed). Right now reset assumes quotas are already correct.

Logan Wright: For headroom calc: we can’t perfectly estimate tokens/min in real time, but we *can* read limiter counters + recent throttle events and report “risk high”. I’ll draft a simple heuristic: if background traffic > 60% of limit over last 5 min => warn/fail.

Mei Lin: Re: traffic generator preset: currently set to keep dashboards “pretty” (lots of endpoints). I can create a “low-baseline” preset for business hours + a “warm dashboards” burst that SE can trigger 10 min pre-demo.

Talia Benson: I’ll align w/ Markus on a booking/slots doc + interim convention (per-AE projects) until ENG-4894 is fully shipped. Also will update the demo certification checklist to include running healthcheck.

Mina Haddad: Slight add: if we’re failing over models/regions during the reliability portion, that can spike retries and amplify rate-limit usage. Maybe healthcheck should also confirm fallback policy isn’t generating retry storms (or at least surface retry rate).

Sean Gallagher: Good call on retries. Let’s add to healthcheck: “retry rate last 5 min” (or “requests per successful completion”) and flag if it’s elevated.

Allison Grant: I’ll add a demo-only dashboard panel: 429 rate, retry rate, and limiter utilization. If we can land that, SEs can screenshot it when something goes wrong.

Ethan Park: Owner/date confirm:
- Quota defaults: I can make the config change today + get it into the demo bootstrap by Thursday.

Devon Price: Works. I’ll open a PR to the bootstrap CLI to apply quotas and print them at the end (so SE sees what they’re running with).

Markus Klein: For the runbook: I’ll add “pause synthetic traffic” step + “if 429: reduce concurrency, confirm quotas, run healthcheck, then escalate” with who to ping.

Sean Gallagher: Perfect. I’ll update SUP-4127 with these action items and link any PRs. Also: please keep this thread updated when the changes land so we can close the PIR.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Status update requested. Remember to post mitigation + follow-up items in-thread for auditability.

Sean Gallagher: Last note: Let’s target having a “demo preflight PASS/FAIL” experience that takes <60s. If it takes longer than the demo itself, people will skip it.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: I’ll keep the output super terse: `PASS` or `FAIL` plus a single-line reason + link to runbook.

Mei Lin: I’ll also add a simple command for SEs: `demo-traffic pause` / `demo-traffic resume` (even if it’s just a wrapper around the job toggle). If that’s too much, at least a documented console button.

Sean Gallagher: Closing the loop: thanks all. Action items confirmed. I’ll check back next week to confirm healthcheck + quota updates are live.
